topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, introduces complement as a challenging but essential topic, and sets the scope of the session.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals, nomenclature, and central C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational principles of the complement cascade, including its general functions, naming conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways that recognize pathogens and drive complement activation toward a concentrated trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream effector processes through which activated complement eliminates pathogens, including opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host cells from unintended complement destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct medical pathologies and disease presentations resulting from specific complement protein deficiencies.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms used by pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus to circumvent complement defenses.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
